newsitem.title: EGYPT: New U.S. building technique coming to Egypt.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. building technique coming to Egypt.

text.p: International Business Organisation (IBO), a private partnership based in California, is transferring to Egypt a construction technique for which it has bought the patent, IBO chairman said on Monday.
"This technique of prefabricated 'sandwiches' or panels insulated by special autofrost foam has been applied in the United States only four months ago," chairman Ashraf al-Desouky told Reuters.
"It is the result of several years of development by construction expert Frank Store, owner of E.E. System," Desouky added. "IBO has bought the patent and Store's only plant."
Prefab units, which can be built without concrete supports up to to 30 metres (100 feet) high, are fireproof and resistant to earthquakes, IBO vice president William Kent said.
"This technology exists only in the United States and its cost is 40 percent less than conventional building techniques," Kent added.
The Egyptian side of the partnership is the Misr Far East Company for Investments.
The two top IBO executives declined to give the cost of the agreement, signed on the margins of an Egyptian-Asian seminar which opened in Cairo on Sunday.
But sources close to the joint venture, called Advanced Building Concepts (ABC), said the preliminary investment was close to $1 million, excluding the cost of land.
"We forecast that ABC sales over three years will be worth one billion Egyptian pounds," he added.
The joint venture, which includes two plants, one to produce the foam and the other for building prefabricated partitions, will start production in three or four months, Desouky said.
The first stage of ABC, to be set up on an area of 20,000 square metres (five acres), has an annual capacity of 6,000 housing units and will employ 120 workers.
"A new production line, with 120 new jobs, will be added every three to four months, if demand justifies," Desouky said.
"Statistics show that the Middle East, excluding Israel, needs 17 million housing units up till the year 2000 and out of this three million units are needed in Egypt.
"This is not to mention factories and hospitals," he added.
Misr Far East holds 60 percent of ABC, and IBO holds the remaining 40 percent.
